QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_14

question.text: A rural maternal-health programme reports a 60% reduction in maternal mortality in beneficiary villages. Before accepting this figure, the SIA should FIRST:

answer.text: Accept the figure if signed off by the CFO of the SE
Verify the baseline data, sample size, data quality, assumptions and limitations before accepting the 60% reduction
Convert the 60% into a monetised figure and include it in the impact ratio
Benchmark against the national average and adopt whichever is higher

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook stresses the importance of verifying baseline data, sample size, data quality, assumptions and limitations of the assessment before accepting a reported outcome. These checks protect against accepting an unsupported headline figure. The Trap: Sign-off by a single executive abandons professional scepticism. Monetising the figure before validation jumps past evidence. Indicator-shopping against benchmarks is not a substitute for validation. Note: Always document baseline, sample, data quality and limitations in the report so users can assess the reliability of the reported reduction.
